statements.statement: Good programmers never create bugs in their code.
statements.explanation: Every programmer creates bugs, and it is completely normal. Even the best programmers in the world introduce bugs regularly. What matters is the ability to find and fix them.

statements.statement: Debugging means tracking down what went wrong in your code and fixing it.
statements.explanation: Debugging is the detective work of finding the source of a problem and correcting it. It is a core part of programming, not a sign that something went wrong.

statements.statement: Experienced programmers spend more time debugging than writing new code.
statements.explanation: Even the best programmers spend a large portion of their time debugging. Writing new code is only part of the job. Understanding and fixing unexpected behavior is where much of the real work happens.

statements.statement: A bug means the programming language itself is broken.
statements.explanation: A bug is when your program does something you did not intend. It is a mistake in your instructions, not a flaw in the language. The language did exactly what you told it to do; the problem is that you told it the wrong thing.
